rows.difficultyReason: Construct and evaluate an exponential CDF, invert it for the median, and interpret a restricted sample space to form an interval probability divided by F(8). The parts guide a prepared student through linked procedures.

derivation.a: For t<0, F(t)=0; for t>=0, integrating (2/5) exp(-2x/5) from 0 to t gives F(t)=1-exp(-2t/5). The CDF is continuous at 0, nondecreasing, and tends to 1 at infinity.
derivation.c: Set 1-exp(-2m/5)=1/2; m=(5/2) ln 2=1.73286795... minutes, approximately 1.73 minutes.
derivation.d: The intersection of T>3 with T<8 is 3<T<8. Continuity makes endpoint conventions immaterial; [F(8)-F(3)]/F(8)=[exp(-6/5)-exp(-16/5)]/[1-exp(-16/5)]=0.27149890..., or 0.27 to 2 decimal places.

rows.sourceAndNativeReview: The complete stem and all four source parts are preserved in order; exam allocation marks are omitted. Each native worked solution preserves the supplied source solution, and all four short answers are mathematically equivalent. The explicit two-decimal instruction for (d) is retained and met; the other approximations retain exact expressions. The density has support t>=0 and integrates to 1.

variantMethodMapping.explanation: For the supplied CDF, F(3)=12/16 and F(4)=15/16; because A<=3 is contained in A<=4, the conditional probability is F(3)/F(4)=0.8. The selected NSG 2023 whole covers the same conditional-ratio method with an interval intersection; the previously accepted piecewise-density/graph/median and CDF representatives cover the other stated method demands.
